inlines.text: A kite is flying at a height of 45 m above the ground at the end of a string of length 70 m. Find the angle of elevation from the ground to the string. Answer to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Right triangle retaining the string, vertical height, horizontal ground, theta and right-angle marker. Decorative kite omitted; ordinary source-green geometry rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The hypotenuse is 70 m and the side opposite theta is 45 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied demonstration diagram.

answer.worked: $$\color{#268cff}\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{45}{70}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{45}{70}\right)\\\theta&\approx40^\circ\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: A kite is flying at a height of 35 m above the ground at the end of a string of length 60 m. Find the angle of elevation from the ground to the string, answer to the nearest minute.

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{35}{60}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{35}{60}\right)\\\theta&\approx35.6853347^\circ\\\theta&\approx35^\circ41'\end{aligned}$$

inlines.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a flagpole from the ground, as observed from a point 15 m from its base, is 63°. Find the height of the flagpole to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Vertical pole, dashed horizontal ground and dashed line of sight, with source labels. Decorative flag omitted; ordinary source-green lines rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The pole height x is opposite the 63-degree elevation angle; adjacent horizontal distance is 15 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied demonstration diagram.

answer.worked: $$\color{#268cff}\begin{aligned}\tan(63^\circ)&=\frac{x}{15}\\15\tan(63^\circ)&=x\\x&\approx29.4\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: The angle of elevation of the top of a flagpole from the ground, as observed 50 m from its base, is 38°. Find the height of the flagpole to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the height of the flagpole.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan(38^\circ)&=\frac{x}{50}\\50\tan(38^\circ)&=x\\x&\approx39.1\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

inlines.text: The angle of depression from the top of a vertical cliff, 150 m above sea level, to a boat below is 50°. Find the distance of the boat from the base of the cliff to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Cliff triangle with both 50-degree angles, upper horizontal reference, sea-level baseline, height and distance labels, and two right-angle markers. Contextual cliff, sea and boat artwork omitted.
spec.mathematics: Parallel horizontal lines give equal depression and elevation angles. The height is 150 m and the horizontal distance is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied demonstration diagram, including both supplied angle labels.

answer.worked: $$\color{#268cff}\begin{aligned}\tan(50^\circ)&=\frac{150}{x}\\x&=\frac{150}{\tan(50^\circ)}\\x&\approx126\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: The angle of depression from the top of a vertical cliff, 135 m above sea level, to a boat below is 37°. Find the distance of the boat from the base of the cliff to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
The angle of elevation from the boat is $37^\circ$ because alternate angles on parallel horizontal lines are equal. Let $x$ metres be the horizontal distance from the cliff base to the boat.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan(37^\circ)&=\frac{135}{x}\\x&=\frac{135}{\tan(37^\circ)}\\x&\approx179\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Identify the right triangle and unknown, select sine or tangent, substitute the given measurements, then use inverse sine or rearrange the ratio. Convert decimal degrees to degrees and minutes for the kite response. Depression and elevation angles are equal by alternate angles on parallel horizontal lines.

A fishing boat starts from point $O$ and sails 75 km on a bearing of $160^{\circ}$ to point $B$.
How far east of its starting point is the boat, to the nearest kilometre?

spec.description: Blank four-direction compass rose. No point, route, distance or angle is supplied.
spec.mathematics: North is up and east is right.
spec.answerVisibility: Blank student drawing scaffold only.

answer.worked:
The angle between the route and south is $180^{\circ}-160^{\circ}=20^{\circ}$. Let $x$ km be the distance east.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin20^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{75}\\x&=75\sin20^{\circ}\\x&\approx26\text{ km}\end{aligned}$$
The boat is 26 km east of its starting point, to the nearest kilometre.
